name: heavy_transcendental_1d
targeted_gap: Heuristic assumes pointwise==bandwidth-bound; a flat kernel can be pure-ALU compute-bound where the big bandwidth tile is the WRONG objective.
hypothesis: 1 bf16 load + 1 bf16 store => bytes_per_elem=4 => budget_target=8192//4=2048, reg_cap huge => seed tiles [2048]. Default is [32]. The chain has ~30 chained transcendentals (exp/log/tanh/sin/cos/erf/div) so it is ALU-bound, not HBM-bound. With num_warps FIXED at 4, a 2048-elem program gives each of 4 warps ~16 serial elements of the deep transcendental pipeline, occupying only ~4 warps per SM and serializing the long-latency SFU ops; the default [32] launches 64x more programs => far more warps in flight => far better SFU/ALU latency hiding. Expect seed >10% slower.
code:
@helion.kernel()
def heavy_transcendental_1d(x):
    out = torch.empty_like(x)
    for t in hl.tile(x.size(0)):
        v = x[t].to(torch.float32)
        v = torch.sin(v) + torch.cos(v * 1.3)
        v = torch.tanh(v) - torch.tanh(v * 0.7)
        v = torch.exp(-v * v)
        v = torch.log(v + 2.0) / (torch.exp(v) + 1.0)
        v = torch.erf(v) + torch.sin(v * 2.1)
        v = torch.tanh(v) * torch.cos(v)
        v = torch.exp(v) / (torch.exp(-v) + 3.0)
        v = torch.log1p(torch.abs(v)) + torch.sin(v)
        v = v / (torch.cos(v) * torch.cos(v) + 1.5)
        v = torch.tanh(torch.exp(-torch.abs(v)))
        v = torch.erf(v * 0.9) - torch.sin(v)
        v = torch.exp(v) / (torch.log(torch.abs(v) + 2.0) + 1.0)
        out[t] = v.to(out.dtype)
    return out
def make_inputs(shape):
    (N,) = shape
    return (torch.randn(N, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16),)

name: chained_activation_2d
targeted_gap: 2-D flat kernel: heuristic distributes a large bandwidth tile innermost-first, but a deep transcendental chain makes it ALU-bound so the wide inner tile at 4 warps under-occupies vs the [32,32]-default's many programs.
hypothesis: 2 bf16 loads + 1 bf16 store => bytes_per_elem=6 => budget_target=8192//6=1365 => pow2-floored inner => seed distributes [1,1024] (innermost absorbs, outer stays 1). Default is [32,32]. The body chains ~25 transcendentals so it is SFU/ALU-bound; a [1,1024] program with fixed 4 warps hides SFU latency across only ~4 warps, while [32,32]=1024 elems in the SAME shape but spread over MANY more programs => higher warp-level parallelism per SM. Same total work, but the seed's single wide row per program starves occupancy of the long transcendental pipeline. Expect seed >10% slower.
code:
@helion.kernel()
def chained_activation_2d(x, y):
    out = torch.empty_like(x)
    for tm, tn in hl.tile(x.size()):
        a = x[tm, tn].to(torch.float32)
        b = y[tm, tn].to(torch.float32)
        v = torch.sin(a) * torch.cos(b) + torch.tanh(a - b)
        v = torch.exp(-v * v) + torch.erf(v * 0.5)
        v = torch.log(torch.abs(v) + 1.5) / (torch.exp(v) + 2.0)
        v = torch.tanh(v) - torch.sin(v * 1.7) * torch.cos(v * 0.9)
        v = torch.exp(v) / (torch.exp(-v) + 4.0)
        v = torch.erf(v) + torch.log1p(torch.abs(v))
        v = v / (torch.cos(v) * torch.cos(v) + 1.25)
        v = torch.tanh(torch.exp(-torch.abs(v))) + torch.sin(v)
        v = torch.exp(-torch.abs(v)) * torch.erf(v * 1.1)
        v = torch.log(torch.abs(v) + 2.0) - torch.tanh(v)
        out[tm, tn] = v.to(out.dtype)
    return out
def make_inputs(shape):
    M, N = shape
    return (torch.randn(M, N, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16),
            torch.randn(M, N, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16))

name: iterated_map_fp32
targeted_gap: fp32 storage + a VERY deep transcendental chain: reg_bytes_per_elem stays small (flat slab=1) so reg_cap does NOT bind, and the byte model still picks a large tile that spills the deep fp32 live set and cannot hide SFU latency at 4 warps.
hypothesis: 1 fp32 load + 1 fp32 store => bytes_per_elem=8 => budget_target=8192//8=1024; reg_bytes_per_elem=2*4=8 => reg_cap=65536//8=8192 (does NOT bind); so seed tiles [1,1024]. Default is [32,32]. The body is a Newton/transcendental iteration (~40 elementwise ops incl pow/exp/log/div) => extreme arithmetic intensity per byte and a large simultaneously-live fp32 register set. A 1024-wide fp32 program at fixed 4 warps both raises register pressure (spill risk) AND under-occupies the SFU-bound chain vs the many-program [32,32] default. Expect seed >10% slower (or spill).
code:
@helion.kernel()
def iterated_map_fp32(x):
    out = torch.empty_like(x)
    for tm, tn in hl.tile(x.size()):
        v = x[tm, tn].to(torch.float32)
        r = v * 0.5 + 0.5
        for _ in range(6):
            r = 0.5 * (r + (torch.abs(v) + 1e-3) / (torch.abs(r) + 1e-3))
        w = torch.exp(-torch.abs(v)) * torch.sin(v) + torch.cos(v * 1.3)
        w = torch.tanh(w) - torch.erf(w * 0.8)
        w = torch.log(torch.abs(w) + 2.0) / (torch.exp(w) + 1.5)
        w = torch.pow(torch.abs(w) + 1e-3, 1.5) - torch.sin(w * 2.0)
        w = torch.exp(w) / (torch.exp(-w) + 3.0)
        w = torch.tanh(torch.pow(torch.abs(w) + 1e-3, 0.75))
        v = r * torch.cos(w) + w * torch.sin(r)
        v = torch.erf(v) + torch.log1p(torch.abs(v)) - torch.tanh(v)
        out[tm, tn] = v.to(out.dtype)
    return out
def make_inputs(shape):
    M, N = shape
    return (torch.randn(M, N, device='cuda', dtype=torch.float32),)
